This statement is false. The study is observational, not a randomized experiment. A higher incidence in the rosiglitazone group (2,593/67,593 ≈ 3.84%, against 5,386/159,978 ≈ 3.37% for pioglitazone) shows an association. It cannot prove causation, because confounding is possible. For example, doctors may prescribe rosiglitazone to patients who are already at higher risk. A difference in rates also never "proves" anything on its own, since it is subject to sampling variability.

ANSWER: false
